title: NaN compares unequal to itself — X .EQ. X is FALSE when X is NaN
sourceContent:
SUBROUTINE CHECK_FRESH(X, OK)
C     OK is .TRUE. unless X has gone NaN (e.g. via 0.0/0.0 or sqrt
C     of a negative number computed upstream). IEEE 754 says
C     NaN .EQ. NaN is FALSE, so X .EQ. X is a stable NaN detector.
C     Translating to Java's '!Double.isNaN(x)' preserves the meaning;
C     translating to 'x == x' triggers static-analyzer warnings.
      IMPLICIT NONE
      REAL    X
      LOGICAL OK
      OK = (X .EQ. X)
      RETURN
      END
notes: X .EQ. X is the canonical Fortran NaN-detector idiom. A direct port to (x == x) often gets refactored by linters or LLMs to 'true' which silently breaks NaN propagation. The spec must capture the NaN-detector contract AND ask the rewrite to use the language's idiomatic isNaN/isnan function.
